The horizontal wind variance logarithmic increases with height, in direct relation with the friction velocity and roughness length scale, The time integral scale increases with surface roughness and decreases with anemometer height The spectral gap shifts to higher frequencies with surface roughness The spectral peak length scale decreases with surface roughness, The dissipation rate shows a z-less profile under stable conditions.
the horizontal wind variances, the Eulerian time scales, the frequency ranges of turbulence and the dissipation rate of the turbulent kinetic energy are affected by the soil surface roughness.
the horizontal wind turbulence characteristics of the Atmospheric Layer Surface (ASL) are affected by the soil tillage treatment.

understanding the effects of surface roughness and soil tillage on the turbulent flow characteristics of the ASL.

the cup anemometers are not suitable for turbulence studies.
the horizontal wind velocity variance is directly related to the friction velocity, the roughness length, and the height above the ground.

the cup anemometers can only be used in the ASL to obtain information on the wind speed fluctuations at a given level, and that they are not suitable to obtain information about the turbulence characteristics of the flow, such as the turbulent kinetic energy and the turbulent energy dissipation.
